svg.aria-label: A circle with centre O and a tangent XY touching it at P. The radius OP is drawn. A point Q on the tangent lies outside the circle; the dashed segment OQ crosses the circle at R, so OQ is longer than the radius OP. The right angle at P between OP and XY is what Theorem 10.1 proves.
svg.title: Theorem 10.1: the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact
svg.desc: Redrawn as a labelled SVG from NCERT Mathematics Class 10 (Reprint 2026-27), Circles (ch. 10), Fig. 10.5, p.147: circle with centre O, tangent XY at P, radius OP, a point Q on XY other than P joined to O. NCERT's figure labels O, P, Q, X, Y; the point R where OQ meets the circle and the 90-degree mark at P are added here to make the shortest-distance argument readable (OQ = OR + RQ, which is longer than OR = OP).

g.text: OQ = OR + RQ > OR = OP for every point Q of XY other than P
OP is the shortest distance from O to XY ⇒ OP ⊥ XY (Theorem 10.1)
